A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, seven figures, hyperparameter table and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-metric computations and trained-model accuracy on maximum retrieval, second-maximum retrieval and parity, notably in Figures 1, 3 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports self-edge and degree ablations in Section 7 and Wikipedia language-model findings in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The graph-quality measures, Poisson generator and recursive FS construction remain unchanged. Applying the existing graphs as Gemma attention masks extends evaluation; the self-edge and degree variations are experimental controls rather than revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic maximum retrieval, second-maximum retrieval and bitstring parity. v2 retains these and adds Wikipedia language modelling with fine-tuned Gemma 2B in Appendix E, substantially extending coverage to natural-language data and prediction.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the same Erdős–Rényi, expander, fully connected, line and Poisson comparators. The added Wikipedia comparison uses the already evaluated fully connected and line graph families; no new comparison algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a distinct evaluation protocol: fine-tuning Gemma 2B for 3,000 batches, applying graph masks across all Transformer layers, and comparing perplexity. Section 7 also adds self-edge and degree controls. The original synthetic-task architectures, training budgets and train/test length ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained FS degree-scaling analysis, v2 reports removing self-edges and comparing O(1), O(log n) and O(sqrt n) in-degrees. These targeted ablations address information retention and degree sensitivity, but are documented only through brief qualitative findings.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains identical shaded bands. v2 adds no run counts, seeds, band definitions, uncertainty-estimation procedures or statistical tests. Its new uses of 'significant' are not accompanied by statistical testing.

E6.justification: Existing plotted results are unchanged. v2 newly reports that removing self-edges harms performance, especially parity; increasing degree improves in-distribution performance without a significant out-of-distribution effect; and Wikipedia perplexity with FS is comparable to fully connected graphs and better than line graphs. These additions contain no numerical scores.

T1.justification: New Proposition 4.2 and Appendix A provide a formal path-count lower bound where v1 offered a conjectural mixing-time discussion. Theorem 6.1's proof replaces simplifying integrality assumptions with floor/ceiling depth accounting and a separate bounding recurrence. v2 also corrects the outdegree inequality in Lemma 4.1's proof and several mathematical expressions, while retaining the stated FS asymptotic bound.

C1.justification: The abstract and central conclusion retain the same contributions: two complementary graph-quality measures, FS graph discovery, theoretical analysis and favorable benchmark performance. The added evidence does not redefine these claims; the introduction makes the existing sequential-data scope more explicit.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes sequential input graphs from general feedforward neural networks such as MLPs. Its conclusion identifies fixed graphs across layers as a boundary and proposes dynamic graphs and a stronger joint framework for the metrics. Section 7 also connects self-edge removal to lost information retention.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly discloses that learning-rate and weight-decay tuning used only fully connected graphs, with parameters reused elsewhere; this does not establish a changed tuning procedure. It also supplies the Wikipedia source link and basic Gemma masking and training-budget details. Existing hyperparameters and Table 1 are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion of directed-graph methods and sparse attention, citing Maskey, Zaheer, and Liao and Póczos, and acknowledges feedforward extenders by Csóka and Grabowski. Lim supports the new future-work discussion, and a separate Gemma reference accompanies the language experiment. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Focused paragraphs expand the introduction, motivation, results and conclusion. A new proof appendix shifts the existing appendices from A–D to B–E. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact; title and heading capitalization and the proceedings notice are updated.

P2.justification: All seven figures and Table 1 are retained without changes to their plotted content or table values. Figures 5–7 are consolidated from two pages onto one gallery page, with additional text and float reflow elsewhere. No figures or result tables accompany the new experiments.

improvement.justification: The added path-count argument, corrections and more explicit FS proof improve theoretical support, while scope clarification and tuning disclosure improve transparency. The ablation and Wikipedia findings broaden empirical support, but their lack of numerical results and detailed protocols limits the gain. The central method and existing quantitative evidence remain unchanged.
